intro: In 2017 Michael Heiser published Reversing Hermon: Enoch, the Watchers, and the Forgotten Mission of Jesus Christ. Its claim is bold. Heiser argued that the New Testament writers knew the old story of the Watchers who came down on Mount Hermon, and of the nations handed to other gods after Babel. He read the life of Jesus and the work of his followers as a plan to undo both.

This unit follows that argument place by place. You will stand at the spring of Pan below Mount Hermon, where Peter spoke about Jesus. You will climb a high mountain with three disciples. Then you will join a festival crowd in Jerusalem and trace Paul's plans all the way to Spain. At each stop you will read the text, hear Heiser's reading, and meet at least one other reading.

By the end, you will be able to explain what Heiser meant by reversing Hermon and by Babel reversed. You will also be able to weigh his readings against others, using manuscripts, places and passages. The aim is not to decide what to believe. It is to read closely and fairly.
bigQuestion: What did Heiser mean by the forgotten mission of Jesus, and how do the texts he used support or challenge his reading?

test.q: What is the subtitle of Heiser's Reversing Hermon (2017)?
choices: Recovering the Supernatural Worldview of the Bible
What the Bible Really Says About God's Heavenly Host
Enoch, the Watchers, and the Forgotten Mission of Jesus Christ
A Reader's Commentary on the Book of the Watchers
test.why: The full title is Reversing Hermon: Enoch, the Watchers, and the Forgotten Mission of Jesus Christ; the others belong to his other books.

test.q: Which text says the Watchers swore an oath on Hermon?
test.why: 1 Enoch 6 says the two hundred Watchers came down on Hermon and bound themselves with an oath there.

test.q: At the foot of which mountain was Caesarea Philippi?
test.why: Caesarea Philippi stood at the spring of Panias, below Mount Hermon.

test.q: Which Greek god had a cave shrine at Panias?
test.why: Panias was named for Pan, god of shepherds and wild places, honored at its cave.

test.q: In Matthew 16:18, what will not prevail against the church?
test.why: Jesus says the gates of Hades will not prevail against the church he will build.

test.q: Which reading of the rock is held in Catholic teaching?
test.why: Catholic teaching reads the rock as Peter, with his role continued in the bishops of Rome.

test.q: Why do Heiser and others place the Transfiguration on Hermon?
choices: It comes six days after Caesarea Philippi, at Hermon's foot
test.why: The Gospels do not name the mountain, but the event follows the scene at Caesarea Philippi, below Hermon.

test.q: Which book of the Hebrew Bible tells of the tower of Babel?
test.why: The Babel story is in Genesis 11:1–9, right after the Table of Nations in Genesis 10.

test.q: In Heiser's reading of Deuteronomy 32:8–9, what happened to the nations after Babel?
choices: They were ruled from Mount Sinai
They were placed under lesser elohim, while God kept Israel
test.why: Heiser read the sons of God reading to mean the nations were allotted to lesser heavenly beings, and Israel was kept as God's portion.

test.q: Which word in Acts 2:3 did Heiser link with the Septuagint of Deuteronomy 32:8?
test.why: The tongues of fire are divided (diamerizo), the same verb the Septuagint uses for dividing the nations.

test.q: What other background do many readers see for Pentecost?
choices: The giving of the Law at Sinai
test.why: Jewish tradition linked Shavuot with Sinai, which also had fire, sound and a gathered people.

test.q: How many followers does Luke 10:1 say Jesus sent out?
choices: Seventy or seventy-two, depending on the manuscript
test.why: The manuscripts of Luke 10:1 differ between seventy and seventy-two, matching the Table of Nations counts.

test.q: Which prophet lists Tarshish among far nations in chapter 66 of his book?
test.why: Isaiah 66:19 sends messengers to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan and the coastlands.

test.q: What did Walter Wink argue about the powers?
choices: The language also describes the inner spirit of human institutions
They are the giants of Bashan
test.why: In Naming the Powers (1984), Wink read the powers as including the spirit of institutions such as empires.

test.q: Which statement attributes a view properly?
choices: The Bible proves Pentecost reversed Babel
Acts states in those words that Pentecost reversed Babel
Heiser argued that Pentecost reversed Babel
test.why: Babel reversed is Heiser's reading of Acts 2; other readers stress Sinai, so the view belongs to him.

write.prompt: Did Jesus' mission, as the texts describe it, reverse Hermon and Babel, as Heiser argued? Choose Caesarea Philippi or Pentecost. Cite two or three passages from the unit, such as Matthew 16:18, 1 Enoch 6:6, Deuteronomy 32:8 or Acts 2:3. Explain what each text says, how Heiser read it, and how one other reader reads it.
tips: Name the book, chapter and verse, and the translation or manuscript you use.
Attribute every view: Heiser argued, other scholars read, Catholic teaching holds.
Compare the readings instead of judging which faith is right.
Use unit terms such as Watchers, Septuagint, Table of Nations and Hades.
